usedBeforeIntro.message: „{entity}” is used in {node} before it is introduced (in {at}).
usedBeforeIntro.why: The reader meets it here without knowing what it is; everything must be introduced before it is used.
usedBeforeIntro.fix: Introduce it earlier, move this use after {at}, or mark this place as the introduction.

notIntroducedHere.message: „{entity}” is used in {node}, but on this path it is never introduced (only in: {elsewhere}).
notIntroducedHere.why: Readers of this edition never get the introduction, which stands in a version for others.
notIntroducedHere.fix: Introduce it in this edition too (in the shared core or in this version), or avoid it here.

neverIntroduced.message: „{entity}” is used in {node}, but it is introduced nowhere.
neverIntroduced.why: Everything a reader needs must be introduced before it is used.
neverIntroduced.fix: Mark the place where it is introduced (role „introduced”), or add a section that introduces it.

introducedNotUsed.message: „{entity}” is introduced in {node} but never used afterwards.
introducedNotUsed.why: An introduction that leads nowhere costs the reader attention for nothing.
introducedNotUsed.fix: Use it later, or drop the introduction.

introducedTwice.why: A second introduction confuses: is it something new?
introducedTwice.fix: Keep one introduction; mark the other place as „recalled” or „used”.

prerequisiteLate.message: „{entity}” (in {node}) needs „{needs}”, which is introduced only in {at}.
prerequisiteLate.why: A concept can be understood only after what it builds on.

noDefinition.fix: Mark the place where it is defined (role „defined”).

noExample.fix: Add an example and mark it (role „example”).

phaseInvalid.message: „{entity}” appears in {node}, where none of its phases is valid.
phaseInvalid.why: The person, place or thing is described differently in different parts of the work; here no description holds.
phaseInvalid.fix: Extend the range of a phase to this place, or check whether the right phase is meant.

forbiddenForm.why: The glossary forbids this synonym or form.

newBringsNothing.message: {node} has the role „new” but introduces nothing.
newBringsNothing.why: Every section must bring something new or openly say that it is something else (a summary, a transition …).
newBringsNothing.fix: Mark what it introduces, or change its role.

summaryIntroduces.why: A summary brings nothing new — the reader expects only what they already know.
summaryIntroduces.fix: Introduce „{entity}” earlier, or change the role of {node}.

summaryRecallsUnknown.message: The summary {node} recalls „{entity}”, which has not been introduced before.
summaryRecallsUnknown.why: A summary can only recall what came before.
summaryRecallsUnknown.fix: Introduce „{entity}” before {node}, or drop it from the summary.

lengthOff.why: Units far from their length break the rhythm of the whole (and the time a sermon may take).
lengthOff.fix: Shorten or extend it, or change the target.

noPurpose.why: Without a purpose nobody knows what the reader gains here and why it stands here.
noPurpose.fix: Write in one or two sentences what this section is for.

noRole.why: The role says what the reader is reading: something new, a summary, a transition, an example …

dimensionGap.message: {node} is split by „{dimension}”, but there is nothing for „{value}”.
dimensionGap.why: On this path the reader finds a gap here.
dimensionGap.fix: Add the version for „{value}”, or mark it as deliberately not needed.

templateChanged.message: The template „{template}” has changed since {node} was made from it.
templateChanged.why: The unit may no longer have the shape the template gives.
templateChanged.fix: Apply the template again (missing parts are added; nothing is lost).

templateMissingParts.why: Every unit of the cycle should have the same inner shape.
templateMissingParts.fix: Apply the template to its plan, or write the missing parts.

ruleMaxWords.message: {node} has {words} words, at most {max} are allowed.

ruleMinWords.message: {node} has {words} words, at least {min} are required.

ruleOneNew.message: {node} introduces {count} things; exactly one is expected.
ruleOneNew.fix: Keep one new thought here; move the others.

citationMissing.message: {node} cites „{key}”, which does not exist (or cannot be opened).
citationMissing.why: A citation that does not resolve becomes an empty footnote.
citationMissing.fix: Correct the key or add the source to the Library.

quoteMismatch.message: In {node} the quote „{quote}” does not match the full text in the Library.
quoteMismatch.why: A quote must say exactly what the source says.
quoteMismatch.fix: Correct the quote from the full text.
